chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, who said:

We performed Hajj while we were Muhrim (in the state of pilgrimage), so we walked between As-Safa and Al-Marwah fourteen circuits. We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said, 'There is no harm; seven are for you and seven are discarded.'

key_terms.تُطْرَحُ: Discarded/Supplementary (referring to the extra circuits beyond the obligatory seven)
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: The state of being Muhrim, i.e., in the ritual state of pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to walk more than seven circuits between Safa and Marwah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in the number of circuits during Sa'i, confirming that performing fourteen shawt is valid where the first seven fulfill the obligatory duty and the subsequent seven are considered voluntary (nafl). It reflects the Shia juristic view that extra circuits do not invalidate the ritual but rather add to the spiritual reward, distinguishing between the core obligation and supplementary acts of devotion.
